span.p:
AFTER_CALL_WORK
no new call is offered

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
call record CLOSED
our system's work is finished

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
but the agent may not be free.
Another internal tool. A paper form.
A colleague to ask. A note to write.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: work in systems we do not own

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the agent clicks READY
the ONLY thing that ends ACW

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the ACW timer
may auto-SAVE the record, flagged as timer-ended,
so a call cannot hang open forever.
It must NEVER auto-ready the agent.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
why auto-ready is actively worse. Marking an agent
available while they are mid-task in another system means
the next caller rings an empty desk for a full offer timeout,
then gets re-matched - RONA. A slightly worse utilisation
number is far cheaper than a caller waiting for nobody.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
and it makes the headline metric TRUE. Shrinking ACW is
one of this product's most credible claims. Measuring only
time-in-our-form would let us shrink the number without
shrinking the agent's actual work. End-of-call to
declared-ready measures the real thing.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the risk we accept: an agent who walks away and never
clicks Ready. Handled by SURFACING it - a long-ACW indicator,
supervisor visibility, a nudge after a threshold - never by
the platform asserting an availability nobody confirmed.

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
still one click in the common case:
the workstation offers Save & Ready together.
They only separate when the agent needs them to.
